item.title: LOT-116: member profile screen (from a profile link in the reader)
item.body:
LOT-116
Closes #207
Claim: mac/lot-116

**Problem.** A member profile link in a topic opened the browser; the legacy profile screen (`UserProfileView.swift`, `ProfilViewController.m`) had no port.

**Cause.** Not ported yet; the reader routed `/hfr/profil-<n>.htm` as a plain web link (CHANGELOG-LEGACY row 53).

**Change.**
- `App/SwiftHFR/Profile/`: `UserProfileModel` (`@Observable @MainActor`, `ContentLoader` rules: load once, reload, content kept on a failed reload), `LiveUserProfileSource` (`PageFetcher.profile(as: .anonymous)` + LOT-027 parser; page refused unless served at `https://forum.hardware.fr/hfr/profil-<id>.htm`), `UserProfileView` (sheet: header, figures, sections, smileys, link rows; member text via `Text(verbatim:)`; images through `ReaderImageFetcher`, forum hosts only; links open in a browser per the default-browser setting, never with the session).
- Reader: `ReaderLinkAction.profile(memberID:)` from LOT-095's `.profile` route; `TopicReaderView` presents the sheet; `ReaderServices.profiles` built in `AppEnvironment`. `SafariView` made internal to reuse it.
- MP quick action is an **optional hook** (`onPrivateMessage`), unset here: LOT-128 (#398) wires it; LOT-118 adds the list buttons. Avatar / message-menu entry is LOT-087's.
- Why cookie-less: parser only verified on logged-out captures; logged-in, banned/deleted states are pending capture #124 (spec "Pending capture"). No new HFR fact.
- Spec `docs/lots/LOT-116-user-profile-screen.md`, `App/README.md` row, CHANGELOG-LEGACY row 58 (56 is taken by both #398 and #399).

**Tests** (`App/SwiftHFRTests/Profile/`, `TopicReaderModelTests`), no real HFR traffic:
- `UserProfileSourceTests`: `R56b` fetched once through the cookie-less client only and equal to the parser output; served at another member / home / other host / `http` / other port → `.unreadable`; a topic page → `.unreadable`; offline maps.
- `UserProfileModelTests`: one load on repeated appear; retry after failure; failed reload keeps profile; MP button only with hook and loaded pseudo; links → browser, `javascript:` ignored.
- `TopicReaderModelTests.aProfileLinkOpensTheProfileSheet` (old assertion that a profile is a web link moved to a topic list link).
- Shown to fail with the change reverted (routing line removed, `.authenticated`, URL check removed, `onAppear` guard removed): all 5 targeted tests failed.
- Full app suite green on iPhone 18 Pro and iPad Pro 13" (iOS 27.0) clones; visual check light / dark / XXXL / iPad on anonymized `R56a`/`R56b` through a temporary harness (not committed).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Open member profiles directly from links in forum topics.
  * View profile details, status, summary figures, smileys, and action links, with refresh controls and loading or error feedback.
  * Send a private message from a profile when messaging is available. Profile links open in the app; other web links follow the selected browser setting.
  * Profile requests don’t use account cookies, and links that don’t match the expected profile address are rejected.

* **Documentation**
  * Added documentation for the profile screen and its behavior.

Adds documentation for the profile feature.| **Estimated code review effort:** 3 (Moderate) | ~20 minutes **Change:** Feature ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant TopicReaderView participant TopicReaderModel participant UserProfileModel participant UserProfileView participant LiveUserProfileSource TopicReaderView->>TopicReaderModel: Resolve link TopicReaderModel-->>TopicReaderView: Return profile(memberID) TopicReaderView->>UserProfileModel: Create model with member ID TopicReaderView->>UserProfileView: Present profile sheet UserProfileView->>UserProfileModel: Call onAppear() UserProfileModel->>LiveUserProfileSource: Request profile(memberID:) LiveUserProfileSource-->>UserProfileModel: Return profile or ListLoadError UserProfileModel-->>UserProfileView: Provide profile and loading state ``` **Suggested labels:** `type: lot`
Merge Risk: Low · previous review 0cc68

Some profile links may require extra VoiceOver actions, long smiley codes can be clipped, and failed images may require reopening the sheet. Documentation evidence also remains incomplete.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to 0cc68

The new profile flow keeps account credentials separate from public-profile requests and restricts member-provided content before displaying or opening it. No material security regression was established. Less common profile states remain unverified. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The new attacker-influenced surface is public profile content displayed to a reader who opens a profile link. The inspected wiring does not give that content account-session credentials or native message-sending authority: profile loading is anonymous, and the optional private-message callback is left unset. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — AnonymousTransport uses its own ephemeral session, removes explicit Cookie headers, and disables cookie, credential, and cache storage. Before parsing, the profile source requires the final URL to use HTTPS, the exact forum host, no explicit port or user information, and the requested member's profile path. Final-URL validation occurs after fetching; it is not a per-hop redirect restriction. - _observed_ — Profile identity is established through the validated response URL, not an independently parsed member ID. The parser extracts profile fields without comparing body identity to the request. This is a dependency on the forum's URL-to-content contract, not evidence of an attacker-reachable identity substitution. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _observed_ — Profile images reuse the cookie-less reader image fetcher with third-party access disabled. The fetcher checks policy before every redirect hop, upgrades HTTP requests to HTTPS, limits redirects to five, and caps response bodies at 15 MiB. Refused or failed images remain placeholders. The inherited first-party classification includes qualifying hardware.fr subdomains, not only the two captured image hosts.

**Explanation** The title "LOT-116: member profile screen (from a profile link in the reader)" matches the main change. The PR adds a member profile sheet that opens from profile links in the topic reader, as described in the summary and objectives. The title names the feature and its entry point. The ticket prefix LOT-116 is a work-item label, but the title still states the primary change clearly.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** [`#207`] The changed files map to the profile-screen objective. Profile source, model and view are in `App/SwiftHFR/Profile/`. Reader wiring covers `ReaderLinkAction.profile`, `TopicReaderModel.action(forLink:)`, `TopicReaderView` (sheet presentation and `ReaderServices.profiles`), `AppEnvironment`, and `SafariView` visibility. Tests cover the source, model and reader routing. Documentation covers the LOT-116 spec, the `App/README.md` component row, and the CHANGELOG-LEGACY row. The reader change to profile routing is needed for the sheet to open from topic links. The reported net diff against `dev-swift` is limited to LOT-116's 12 files, and no unrelated change is demonstrated. One documentation inconsistency exists: the PR description cites CHANGELOG-LEGACY row 58, while the generated file summary cites entry 64. This does not establish scope drift.
Full details: Docstring Coverage

**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 54.55% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff with cyclomatic complexity of at least 2. Documentation-only edits and deletions within surviving functions are included; unchanged diff context and fully deleted functions are excluded. Analyzed 11 functions across 10 files. (2 skipped: 2 unsupported.) **Resolution** Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#207`] Coding requirements are implemented at the reviewed head 0cc685c. Evidence: `UserProfileSource.swift` fetches the profile with `fetcher.profile(memberID:, as: .anonymous)` (no cookies), then `UserProfileParser`. It refuses any page whose final URL is not `https://forum.hardware.fr/hfr/profil-<id>.htm` with no port or user info. `UserProfileView.swift` renders all member text with `Text(verbatim:)`, loads images through the cookie-less `ReaderImageFetcher` with `allowsThirdParty: false`, and routes links through the model. The summary and the PR description report `@Observable @MainActor` models, Swift Testing coverage for loading, retry, failed reload, URL validation and link routing, and red-green checks. French UI strings are present ("Fermer", "Actualiser", "Chargement du profil…", "Non renseigné", "Écrire un MP"). Light, dark and XXXL checks are reported. Logged-in, banned and deleted states are deferred by the issue's own condition (capture `#124` pending), so they are not failures. The MP action is an optional hook, and blacklist/whitelist handlers are not present; the PR attributes these to LOT-128 and LOT-118. The acceptance criteria do not name these handlers, so this is not a failure. The remaining open item is the acceptance criterion requiring the `App build + tests` CI job to be green. The PR reports that no pull-request CI ran after the merge with `dev-swift`, and the later source-level review did not run the simulator. No CI result for head 0cc685c is available, so this criterion is unknown. Absence of a run is not evidence of failure.
